skill.name: webask-benchmark
skill.description: Сравнивает результаты опросов WebAsk между собой: одну анкету в разные периоды или разные опросы аккаунта. Применяется, когда человек спрашивает, стало ли лучше, как изменились оценки или какой из опросов работает лучше.
skill.summary: Compare WebAsk survey periods and shared metrics while checking questionnaire changes, response distributions, and sample sizes.
skill.author: webaskio

finding_verdicts.reason: README.md line 1 uses parent-directory paths in HTML breadcrumb links to repository documentation. These are navigation links, not filesystem operations or user-controlled path resolution.
SKILL.md line 23 uses Markdown backticks to name get_quiz_report and describes date-filtered survey retrieval. There is no Ruby code, shell substitution, or instruction to execute a shell command.
SKILL.md line 25 formats get_quiz_list and get_quiz_summary as inline Markdown code for survey retrieval. The text names MCP tools, not shell commands or executable backtick expressions.
SKILL.md line 27 formats get_quiz_versions as an MCP tool name within a questionnaire comparability check. The surrounding prose confirms Markdown formatting rather than Ruby or shell execution.

content.value_statement: Survey scores can mislead when questionnaire changes, sample sizes, and seasonal differences are ignored. This skill guides WebAsk comparisons using version history, response distributions, and shared survey metrics.
actual_capabilities: Guides date-filtered retrieval with get_quiz_report to compare separate periods of one survey.
Uses get_quiz_list and get_quiz_summary to compare shared metrics across account surveys.
Checks get_quiz_versions for questionnaire changes that invalidate direct comparisons.
Compares average ratings, answer distributions, completion rates, and response counts.
Reports change direction and size alongside sample counts, with cautions about small samples and unsupported causal explanations.
Responds in the language used by the requester.
limitations: Requires access to WebAsk survey data and the four declared MCP tools; the skill does not implement those tools.
Different questionnaires support comparisons of shared operational metrics, not answers to different questions.
Provides interpretation guidance but no implemented statistical test or prescribed significance threshold.
Unequal periods, seasonal differences, questionnaire edits, and small samples can prevent reliable conclusions.

use_cases.title: Review Customer Satisfaction Changes
use_cases.description: Compare repeated survey periods to identify rating and distribution changes while checking questionnaire consistency.

use_cases.title: Compare Survey Completion
use_cases.description: Compare completion rates and completion times across account surveys without treating answers to different questions as equivalent.

use_cases.title: Assess Feedback After a Release
use_cases.description: Compare feedback before and after a release while distinguishing observed changes from unproven explanations.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Survey Periods
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [survey] during [period A] and [period B]. Check questionnaire versions and report average ratings, changes, and response counts.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: review one survey across two periods.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Completion Across Surveys
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare completion rates and completion times for [survey A] and [survey B]. Use only shared metrics and explain any comparability limits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: compare operational performance across surveys.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate Distribution Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [survey] across [period A] and [period B]. Check version history, then examine answer distributions, average scores, and sample sizes. Label hypotheses clearly.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: investigate changes that averages may conceal.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Comparison Reliability
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate whether [survey] results from [period A] and [period B] support a reliable comparison. Check questionnaire changes, period lengths, seasonality, and sample sizes. Separate observed differences from unsupported significance or causal claims.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review evidence quality before reporting a trend.

output_examples.input: Illustrative comparison: spring averaged 4.0 from 286 responses; autumn averaged 4.3 from 318 responses. The questionnaire was unchanged.
output: The average increased by 0.3 points, from 4.0 to 4.3.
No questionnaire changes were reported, but seasonal and audience differences still need consideration.
These averages and counts alone do not establish statistical significance or explain the cause.

output_examples.input: Illustrative comparison: two periods use different wording and response options for the satisfaction question.
output: The satisfaction answers are not directly comparable because the question and response options changed.
Do not present the score difference as a satisfaction trend.
Review shared operational metrics separately, with clear comparability caveats.

best_practices: Check questionnaire version history before interpreting changes between survey periods.
Use comparable period lengths and consider seasonal or audience differences.
Report distributions and sample sizes alongside averages, and label explanations that remain hypotheses.
anti_patterns: Treating answers to different questions as directly comparable.
Presenting small score differences as reliable improvement without sufficient evidence.
Interpreting higher response volume as proof of better product quality.

faq.question: What does this skill compare?
faq.answer: It compares one WebAsk survey across periods or shared operational metrics across different surveys in an account.

faq.question: Which tools are required?
faq.answer: It depends on get_quiz_list, get_quiz_report, get_quiz_summary, and get_quiz_versions through MCP.

faq.question: Can it compare surveys with different questions?
faq.answer: It can compare shared metrics such as completion rates and completion times. Answers to different questions are not directly comparable.

faq.question: Does it provide a formal statistical significance test?
faq.answer: No statistical test is implemented or specified. The instructions call for sample-size caution and an assessment of whether differences are meaningful.

faq.question: Does it modify surveys or recommend paid upgrades?
faq.answer: The documented workflow uses retrieval tools. It instructs the assistant to report account limits and stop without recommending payment or plan changes.

faq.question: Which language does it use for responses?
faq.answer: The source instructions are in Russian, but they direct the assistant to respond in the language used by the requester.
